Across the corridors of history, a few extraordinary souls stood against the tides of darkness to bridge fractured worlds. Witness the timeless journeys of legendary Nobel Peace Prize laureates who rewrote the destiny of mankind.

Explore The Laureates

The Five Visionaries

Five lives. Five paths. A lasting influence on human dignity, freedom and peace.

01

Martin Luther King Jr.

Nobel Peace Laureate · 1964

A Baptist minister and central leader of the modern American civil rights movement, who made nonviolent direct action a powerful instrument for democratic change.

“The time is always right to do what is right.”
02

Nelson Mandela

Nobel Peace Laureate · 1993

A South African anti-apartheid leader who spent 27 years in prison and later helped negotiate a democratic transition based on equal political rights.

“It always seems impossible until it’s done.”
03

Mother Teresa

Nobel Peace Laureate · 1979

A Catholic religious sister who founded the Missionaries of Charity and organised care for people living in extreme poverty, illness and abandonment.

“Not all of us can do great things. But we can do small things with great love.”
04

Mahatma Gandhi

Global Icon of Nonviolence · Not a Nobel Laureate

An Indian lawyer and independence leader who developed mass campaigns of nonviolent resistance against racial discrimination and British colonial rule.

“The best way to find yourself is to lose yourself in the service of others.”
05

Malala Yousafzai

Nobel Peace Laureate · 2014

A Pakistani education activist who spoke out for girls’ right to attend school, survived an assassination attempt and became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

“One child, one teacher, one book, one pen can change the world.”

How to activate public video uploads (free setup)

This HTML file cannot store a video online for every visitor by itself. To enable shared uploads, create a free project at Supabase, create a public Storage bucket named peace-videos, and create a table named videos with columns: id (uuid, primary key, default gen_random_uuid()), title (text), storage_path (text), public_url (text), user_id (uuid), and created_at (timestamptz, default now()). Enable Row Level Security.

Then paste your Project URL and anon/publishable key into the two constants SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY near the end of this HTML file. Never put a service-role secret key in a public website.

Create the videos table and enable its security rules:

create table if not exists public.videos (
 id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
 title text not null,
 storage_path text not null unique,
 public_url text not null,
 user_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
 created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table public.videos enable row level security;

Suggested database policies:

create policy "Anyone can view videos" on public.videos
for select using (true);
create policy "Signed-in users can publish" on public.videos
for insert to authenticated with check (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "Owners can delete their videos" on public.videos
for delete to authenticated using (auth.uid() = user_id);

Storage policies for the public bucket: allow public SELECT; allow authenticated INSERT when the first folder name equals auth.uid()::text; allow authenticated DELETE under the same owner-folder condition. The upload code stores each user’s files under their own user ID folder. Configure email confirmation in Supabase Auth as desired.

Copy-ready Storage SQL (run once in Supabase SQL Editor):

insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values ('peace-videos', 'peace-videos', true, 524288000,
array['video/mp4','video/webm','video/ogg','video/quicktime'])
on conflict (id) do update set public = true;

create policy "Public can watch peace videos" on storage.objects
for select using (bucket_id = 'peace-videos');

create policy "Signed-in users upload to own folder" on storage.objects
for insert to authenticated with check (
 bucket_id = 'peace-videos' and
 (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
);

create policy "Users delete only their own videos" on storage.objects
for delete to authenticated using (
 bucket_id = 'peace-videos' and
 (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
);

Also create the public.videos table with the columns listed above and apply the three table policies. Keep your project key public/anon only; never publish a service-role key.

After adding those settings and policies, account registration, public viewing, upload and owner-only deletion become available across devices. The account owner is the only person offered a delete control for their own uploads.
